subject: Re: Stellaris - sizing confirmation & temporary capacity hold request
messages:
From: Avery Singh <avery@stellaris.ai>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial sizing ask for late-stage POC (Stellaris)

Neha — thanks again for the demo yesterday. The exec team wants a short technical note so procurement can start the paperwork. We expect a POC footprint of ~16 A100-equivalent GPUs for the first month (burstable to 32 for synthetic load tests). Can Redwood confirm whether you can "soft-hold" that capacity while legal and procurement finish the SOW? If helpful attached is our internal estimate.

Key asks: 
- Temporary hold on 16 GPUs in us-west for 30 days
- Option to burst to 32 for up to 48 hours during validation windows
- SLA exception: 99.5% latency SLO during test windows

Avery Singh
Head of Infrastructure, Stellaris AI
[Attachment: stellaris_capacity_request.xlsx (spreadsheet, 38KB)]

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Avery Singh <avery@stellaris.ai>, procurement@stellaris.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial sizing ask for late-stage POC (Stellaris)

Avery — thanks for sending this over and for the time yesterday. Looping in Marcus (capacity planning) and Ben (sales ops) to confirm availability and the approval path for a temporary hold.

High level: we can provision a 16-GPU dedicated pool in us-west as a provisional hold. Burst to 32 is possible subject to fleet pressure; that part will require an operational pre-check and an approval window. SLA exception requests need a separate approvals flow (legal + infra) — include any wording you want to see in the SOW so we can route it.

Next steps: Marcus, can you run an availability check for the week of Jan 4, and flag any conflicts? Ben — if we can do a 30-day soft-hold, what booking/commitment language should we ask procurement for?

— Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai

Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 13:27:00 -08:00

On Fri, Dec 18, 2026 at 11:03 AM neha_kapoor@redwood.ai wrote:
> Avery — thanks for sending this over and for the time yesterday. Looping in Marcus (capacity planning) and Ben (sales ops) to confirm availability and the approval path for a temporary hold.
> 
> High level: we can provision a 16-GPU dedicated pool in us-west as a provisional hold. Burst to 32 is possible subject to fleet pressure; that part will require an operational pre-check and an approval window. SLA exception requests need a separate approvals flow (legal + infra) — include any wording you want to see in the SOW so we can route it.

Quick availability readout: we have a narrow window Jan 4–11 with room for a 16-GPU allocation in us-west-2 provided we commit a soft booking by Dec 22. The burst to 32 is not guaranteed — we have a competing commitment on Jan 8–9 but we can reserve headroom if Stellaris signs a short burst addendum.

Operational caveats: 
- We recommend a reserved pool with prefix caching enabled to reduce cold-starts during the validation runs.
- If you need the 32-GPU burst for the synthetic stage, we require a 48-hour notice to pre-warm nodes.

I can hold a provisional booking in the inventory system for 14 days once Ben triggers the request (internal ticket). Please advise if you want me to create the ticket now.

— Marcus Lin
Capacity & Runtime Planning, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: capacity_snapshot_us-west-20261218.pdf (pdf, 12KB)]

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai

Cc: Avery Singh <avery@stellaris.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 08:14:00 -08:00

On Fri, Dec 18, 2026 at 1:27 PM marcus_lin@redwood.ai wrote:
> Quick availability readout: we have a narrow window Jan 4–11 with room for a 16-GPU allocation in us-west-2 provided we commit a soft booking by Dec 22. The burst to 32 is not guaranteed — we have a competing commitment on Jan 8–9 but we can reserve headroom if Stellaris signs a short burst addendum.

I've created the internal hold ticket (HOLD-9123) and set an expiry for 14 days (expires 2026-12-29). To convert this to a 30-day soft-hold we need a signed MOU or a short service addendum that confirms the provisional allocation and the burst clause. Procurement language suggestion: 

"Redwood will provision a provisional allocation of 16 GPUs in us-west-2 for a period of 30 days pending final execution of the SOW. During this period, Stellaris may request up to 32 GPUs for up to 48 consecutive hours with 48 hours' advance notice, subject to Redwood's capacity availability. Redwood will provide best-effort support to honor burst requests but does not guarantee availability during overlapping committed events."

If procurement agrees to that phrasing, I can attach a one-paragraph addendum and route to legal for a quick sign-off. Marking Ben to approve creation of the hold now: HOLD-9123 created. Marcus — please set inventory state to "provisional-held".

— Ben Carter
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

Avery — quick update from our side: we've provisionally placed HOLD-9123 for a 16-GPU pool in us-west-2 (status: provisional-held). Marcus added the inventory note and we uploaded the capacity snapshot. To proceed to a full 30-day soft-hold we need: 

1) Procurement to sign the one-paragraph addendum (Ben attached suggested text below).
2) DocuSign link or signed MOU so we can extend HOLD-9123 to 30 days and set the burst headroom.
3) Confirmation of the validation window(s) (proposed: Jan 6–7 for integration, Jan 10 for synthetic load).

I've attached the SLA-exception instructions we discussed; legal will need to review the latency clause. If you can return the signed addendum by EOD Dec 22 we'll lock the 30-day soft-hold and pre-warm nodes ahead of Jan 4.

Ben — please confirm you pushed the addendum to legal and share the DocuSign link when ready. Marcus — keep the provisional state until we receive the signed doc.

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SLA-exception-approval.pdf (pdf, 9KB)]
